result.title: SpatialScout: Can VLM Agents Actively Explore and Map 3D Scenes?
result.summary: Spatial intelligence requires agents to actively acquire visual evidence and integrate observations into a coherent representation of the three-dimensional world. Yet spatial question answering offers limited evidence of whether models can construct accurate metric maps through autonomous exploration. We introduce SpatialScout, a benchmark for evaluating vision-language model (VLM) agents on active object-level 3D mapping. SpatialScout comprises 80 diverse indoor scenes containing 3,140 target objects. Given an object inventory, RGB observations, camera calibration, and camera poses, agents control a camera to explore each scene and estimate object centers in a shared coordinate frame. The task requires coordinating viewpoint selection, cross-view association, geometric estimation, and map revision under bounded interaction budgets. Evaluation jointly measures localization accuracy and target coverage through object-scale overlap scores that penalize missing predictions. Experiments with frontier VLMs reveal substantial limitations: the strongest evaluated model, Claude Opus 5.5, achieves a mean overlap score of 41.71%, with 47.23% of targets exceeding an intersection-over-union (IoU) threshold of 0.5 and only 3.25% exceeding 0.9. These results reveal a substantial gap between recovering coarse object layouts and constructing complete, precise metric maps. SpatialScout provides a quantitative testbed for developing agents that build reliable 3D spatial representations through active perception. Code is available at https://github.com/JesseZZZZZ/SpatialScout.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 SpatialScout 基准，让 VLM agent 在 80 个室内场景、3140 个目标上主动控制相机探索，并在统一坐标系中估计物体中心；以目标尺度 IoU 重叠与覆盖率联合评分，显示前沿模型只能恢复粗略布局、难以构建精确度量地图。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接涉及主动获取视觉证据、跨视角关联与有限交互预算下的表示构建，可供核查 LVR 中视觉证据筛选、动态计算与停止决策的评价方式，以及 3D 空间表示是否真正保留任务必要信息。
